Marketing & Design Strategy
02 / ORIGIN STORY

From music composition to exam prep

We didn't start here. Two music-tech ideas ran into real-world limits before we found the problem worth solving.

  • 01

    AI-assisted music composition software. Our first idea — helping composers write with AI.

  • 02

    SongCanvas. A networking-based app connecting composers with musicians.

  • 03

    Issues arose: was this a true pain point? Copyright concerns, user acquisition, and scalability all worked against us.

  • 04

    A new focus within EdTech. We pivoted toward a problem every student actually has.

  • 05

    Fundamental problem: a lack of tailored study resources for exam prep, and ineffective ways to ingest and absorb lecture and course materials.

03 / SOLUTION

Our Solution

An AI tool for transforming the way students engage with course content and prepare for exams.

04 / USER RESEARCH

User interviews & market validation

Five themes emerged across student interviews — cautious optimism, paired with real concerns about depth and personalization.

"I will use it for time management but want concise, detailed summaries."

"I prefer writing my own cheat sheets but will use the platform if it has a better UI than Canvas."

"I want the platform to tailor to different learning styles and be customizable."

"A positive secondary resource for quick help, but not a primary tool."

"Concerns about thoroughness and limited customization for individual needs."

08 / VALIDATION

Pretotyping & Product Testing

Condensify Company Overview
09 / SOCIAL MEDIA ENGAGEMENT

Testing demand before building

A mocked social post and waiting list drove 200 upvotes and real email signups — validating demand before writing a line of code.

10 / PRETOTYPES

Simulating the product before it existed

Two "Wizard of Oz" pretotypes — a hand-simulated short-form video and a hand-simulated lecture summary — tested with real participants.

Mechanical Turk — Short Video Generation

A sample short-form video simulating what our AI engine would eventually generate, sourced from "How to Attend Conferences & Build Your Network" (Eesley). Shown to a select group of participants and iterated on their feedback.

The Impersonator — Lecture Notes Generation

We used ChatGPT to hand-craft a tailored example of what a Condensify summary could look like, demonstrating our platform's fundamental advantages before it was built — then iterated on participant feedback.

11 / PROGRESSIVE PRODUCT TESTING

Real feedback, in the margins

Direct annotations from usability sessions shaped everything from naming conventions to processing speed.

13 / COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE

Content summarizers. Video generators. Never both.

Mindgrasp, Coral, Notta, NoteGPT, and Scholarcy summarize content. Veed.io, InVideo, and Synthesia generate video. Nobody combines summarization, microlearning video, and an AI tutor in one platform — with a native Canvas scraper.

  • Coursepage (Canvas) scraper
  • Microlearning short-form video generator
  • Content summarizer, microlearning video platform, & AI tutor — all in one
14 / FUNDING & PARTNERSHIPS

Angel investors, EdTech VCs, and platform partners

Angel investors to build our MVP; EdTech-focused VCs like Owl Ventures and Reach Capital to scale; direct partnerships with Canvas and Quizlet to plug into existing student workflows.

15 / SOCIAL IMPACT & RISKS

What could go wrong

01

Scalability Costs

Scaling media hosting raises costs as users grow.

02

Content Accuracy & Reliability

Accurate AI content is crucial for trust in high-stakes academics.

03

Complexity of Personalization

Tailoring to diverse learning needs adds real engineering complexity.

04

Stakeholder Resistance

Adapting to diverse learning needs complicates AI development.

05

Market Saturation

Standing out in a crowded education market demands costly marketing.

06

Niche Subject Gaps

Supporting diverse courses adds complexity and risks gaps in niche subjects.

17 / TEAM & HIRING

What it takes to build this

Skills Required

  • Advanced NLP techniques for summarizing and synthesizing textual content
  • Transformer-based models (GPT, BERT) for customization and content generation
  • Multimodal AI for handling video, lecture slides, and text documents
  • Automated video processing, including short-form video creation
  • Video summarization algorithms tailored to specific learning styles

Strategies To Attract Talent

  • Professional growth on cutting-edge AI and EdTech projects
  • Connections across EdTech, AI, and academic communities
  • A fast-paced, innovative, entrepreneurial culture
  • Competitive salaries alongside equity in the company
